provenance_quote: This analysis identified 16 new putative T2S substrates, including ... three hypothetical proteins encoded by VCA0583, VCA0738, and VC2298
notes: Sikora 2011 JBC (doi:10.1074/jbc.M110.211078, PMID 21385872) abstract lists VC2298 among 16 new T2S substrates. UniProt Q9KPR8 = VC_2298 'Lipoprotein, putative', V. cholerae N16961 - gene/locus/organism match. Crossref title 'Proteomic Analysis of the V. cholerae Type II Secretome'.

provenance_quote: This analysis identified 16 new putative T2S substrates, including sialidase ... TagA-related protein, cytolysin
notes: Sikora 2011 JBC abstract lists 'TagA-related protein' among new T2S substrates. UniProt Q9KN18 = TagA-related protein, VC_A0148, V. cholerae N16961; genome NC_002506.1 = V. cholerae chromosome II (verified via NCBI esummary) consistent with VC_A0148. Identity OK.

provenance_quote: there is only one Hxc-dependent substrate, namely LapA, known as low-molecular weight alkaline phosphatase
notes: Filloux 2011 Front Microbiol review (Crossref: 'Protein Secretion Systems in Pseudomonas aeruginosa') states LapA is the Hxc (T2SS) substrate. UniProt P35482 = lapA/PA0688, P. aeruginosa PAO1, kw Secreted, secretion 'hxc-dependent', Type II secretion. Identity OK.

provenance_quote: achieves the secretion of all Xcp substrates but the aminopeptidase PaAP
notes: Filloux 2011 review names PaAP an Xcp (T2SS) substrate. UniProt Q9HZQ8 = lap/PA2939 'Aminopeptidase (PaAP)', P. aeruginosa PAO1, kw Secreted, secretion via type II secretion system. Identity OK.

provenance_quote: we identified and characterized plaA, a gene encoding a phospholipase A that cleaves fatty acids from lysophospholipids
notes: Flieger 2002 IAI (Crossref title 'Characterization of the Gene Encoding the Major Secreted Lysophospholipase A of L. pneumophila') confirms plaA is the T2S-secreted lysophospholipase A. But ledger UniProt Q5ZX07 = lpg0926 (uncharacterized coiled-coil protein), NOT plaA. Correct plaA in Phil-1 = Q5ZRP3 (gene lpg2837, 'lysophospholipase A', RefSeq locus LPG_RS14310 via NCBI GeneID 19834402). Ledger effector_locus LPG_RS04595 corresponds to the lpg0926 region, also wrong. Genome NC_002942.5 (Phil-1) is correct. Protein/secretion claim holds; uniprot+locus corrected.

provenance_quote: four other proteins have been shown to be transported by the T2S machinery, including hemagglutinin protease, chitinase, GbpA, and lipase
notes: Sikora 2011 JBC abstract confirms V. cholerae lipase is T2S-transported. But identity fields are wrong: UniProt Q3BY96 is DELETED ('Not part of a reference proteome'); genome NC_007508.1 = Xanthomonas euvesicatoria 85-10 (NCBI esummary), NOT V. cholerae; locus IS_RS03910 is not a V. cholerae locus. Correct V. cholerae N16961 lipase = P15493 (gene lipA/hlyC, VC_A0221, 'Triacylglycerol lipase / Extracellular lipase', kw Secreted/Signal; RefSeq locus VC_RS14395 via NCBI GeneID 2612550). Real T2S substrate, multiple identity fields stale -> fix.

provenance_quote: Aeromonas spp. secrete the channel-forming protein proaerolysin across their inner and outer membranes in separate steps using the general secretion pathway
notes: Letellier 1997 JBC (Crossref 'Studies on the Energetics of Proaerolysin Secretion across the Outer Membrane of Aeromonas') confirms proaerolysin secreted via the general secretion pathway (= T2SS). UniProt P09167 = aerA 'Aerolysin', A. hydrophila, kw Secreted/Signal/Virulence. Identity OK.

provenance_quote: We identified three proteins, ChiY, EngY (YE2830) and YE3650, that are secreted depending on a functional Yts1 T2SS in response to MgCl(2) at low temperature
notes: Shutinoski 2010 Mol Microbiol abstract (PMID 19968791) verbatim confirms YE3650 is a Yts1 (T2SS) secretion substrate. Locus YE_RS18315 / YE3650 confirmed live in Y. enterocolitica 8081 (NCBI GeneID 4714048); genome correct. But UniProt A1JQR7 is DELETED ('Not part of a reference proteome') with no current replacement accession located in UniProt. Real T2S substrate; dead accession -> fix, new_uniprot left blank (no live UniProt entry found).

provenance_quote: we demonstrate that this Txc-secreted substrate binds chitin, and we therefore name it CbpE (chitin-binding protein E)
notes: Cadoret 2014 J Bacteriol abstract (PMID 24748613, PMC4054165) verbatim confirms CbpE is the Txc (third T2SS of PA7) secreted substrate. Locus PSPA7_RS14405 / genome NC_009656.1 (P. aeruginosa PA7) consistent with the paper. But UniProt A6V5Q1 is DELETED ('Not part of a reference proteome'), no current replacement accession located. Real T2S substrate; dead accession -> fix, new_uniprot blank.

provenance_quote: the serine proteases StmPr1 and StmPr2, which were confirmed to be Xps substrates, are predominantly responsible for secreted proteolytic activities exhibited by strain K279a
notes: DuMont 2015 IAI (Crossref 'Type II Secretion-Dependent Degradative and Cytotoxic Activities Mediated by S. maltophilia Serine Proteases StmPr1 and StmPr2') confirms StmPr1 as an Xps (T2SS) substrate. UniProt Q93IQ4 = StmPr1 'Alkaline serine protease', S. maltophilia, kw Secreted/Signal. Identity OK.

provenance_quote: PelI is an extracellular protein secreted by the Out secretory pathway of E. chrysanthemi
notes: Shevchik 1997 J Bacteriol (Crossref 'Pectate lyase PelI of Erwinia chrysanthemi 3937 belongs to a new family') confirms PelI secreted via the Out (T2SS) pathway. UniProt E0SM75 = pelI 'Pectate lyase', D. dadantii 3937 (= E. chrysanthemi 3937), kw Secreted/Signal. Identity OK.
